title: "Updated pollock inputs: what is ready"
date: 2026-10-09
lightbox: true
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)
library(ggthemes)
coverage <- read.csv("site/data/assessment_coverage.csv")
qc <- read.csv("site/data/bts_year_qc.csv")
sheet_audit <- read.csv("site/data/workbook_sheet_audit.csv")
theme_set(ggthemes::theme_few(base_size = 12))
```

## Annual assessment files

```{r}
#| label: tbl-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Coverage is read from file contents; a filename is not an assessment-year declaration."
coverage |>
  select(source, terminal_year, fishery_caa_last, bts_last, ats_last, avo_last) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(source = "Input", terminal_year = "Model end", fishery_caa_last = "Fishery CAA",
             bts_last = "BTS", ats_last = "ATS", avo_last = "AVO")
```

The `pm_25.dat` candidate provides an additional model year, fishery composition,
BTS information, and AVO observation. Its annual weight matrices fail the intake
check: **62 rows are required; fishery weights have 61 and spawning weights have
63**. Reconcile their calendar-year mapping in the source project. Truncation,
repeated terminal weights, or a shift of the row-year alignment would be new
scientific assumptions and must be specified before fitting.

The `pm_26.dat` candidate ends in 2024. The field-by-field comparison finds identical
values for all 53 core fields shared with the RDS cache; the final `test` field
differs in shape. This is a legacy input snapshot, not a completed 2026 update.
The older parser also treats year annotations following comment names as part of
the field name. The audit parser extracts the first header token and checks row
widths, repeated headers, and numeric values.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-weights
#| tbl-cap: "Required and observed annual weight rows."
coverage |>
  select(source, required_weight_rows, fishery_weight_rows, spawning_weight_rows, weight_dimensions_pass) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(source = "Input", required_weight_rows = "Required", fishery_weight_rows = "Fishery",
             spawning_weight_rows = "Spawning", weight_dimensions_pass = "Dimensions pass")
```

## The 2026 BTS workbook

The named sheet `bts_abundance_at_age_1982_2026_` contains ages 1–14 and an explicit
**15+** column. The 2024, 2025, and 2026 rows each have 15 observed cells. Numerical
year filtering excludes trailing scratch calculations labelled `Correc` and blank
rows. The audit retains missing survey years as missing observations.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sheets
#| tbl-cap: "Workbook products have different vintages and one sheet has a broken relationship."
sheet_audit |>
  select(sheet, first_year, last_year, status, warnings_count) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(sheet = "Sheet", first_year = "First year", last_year = "Last year",
             status = "Read status", warnings_count = "Warnings") |>
  sub_missing(missing_text = "—")
```

The `Index` and `AgeComps` products stop in 2024 and include EBS and NBS strata.
The `BTS Natage` sheet fails with a missing `rId3` workbook relationship. Mixed-type
warnings from the older `VAST_ddc_all_2024 CPUE` sheet are recorded in
[workbook warnings](../site/data/workbook_warnings.csv); that sheet is not used for
the current abundance summary. Update biomass indices and uncertainties from an
identified current product, rather than inferring them from the abundance sheet.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bts-recent
#| tbl-cap: "Recent BTS abundance totals from the named 15-age sheet, before assessment integration."
qc |>
  filter(year >= 2024) |>
  mutate(abundance_billions = abundance_total / 1e9) |>
  select(year, cells_observed, abundance_billions, status) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = abundance_billions, decimals = 3) |>
  cols_label(year = "Year", cells_observed = "Observed ages", abundance_billions = "Billion fish", status = "Row status")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bts-age
#| fig-cap: "BTS abundance at age in the 2024–2026 workbook rows. These are survey products, before model fitting."
#| fig-alt: "Three faceted line charts show abundance by age for 2024, 2025, and 2026. The final age is 15 plus. Age profiles differ markedly among years; adjacent totals give numerical summaries."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.8
read.csv("site/data/recent_bts_numbers.csv") |>
  ggplot(aes(age, numbers / 1e9)) +
  geom_line(color = "#176b7b") + geom_point(color = "#176b7b", size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~year, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 15), labels = c("1", "5", "10", "15+")) +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "Billion fish")
```

## Survey weight-at-age

The reviewed VAST-derived weight file covers 1982–2026 with 675 year–age cells,
657 observed weight/SE pairs, and 18 paired missing cells. All 15 cells in 2026
are observed. Units are kg per fish and kg for SE; the stored `cv` is a ratio,
which is multiplied by 100 for a percentage. These are model-derived survey
weights; adoption as final assessment inputs remains unverified.

Fishery weights and a coherent annual assessment input package are still required.
Keep BTS and fishery schedules distinct. The terminal age must continue to mean
15+. Missing survey cells must follow the chosen model's observation rules.

## Model 26.0 reference evidence

Six diagnostic/configuration CSVs were checked against their live counterparts
on the [published September 2026 assessment development site](https://noaa-afsc.github.io/EBS_pollock/doc/EBSpollock_Sept_2026.html).
Five of six differ from the local working copies. The public tables describe a **1964–2024 development fit**, Rceattle **5.23.0**, source commit
`adf22f84b399e84e3b9a707e0b3bbb1624179a27`. This designation describes model
development and does not establish adoption for current advice.

The point estimate has maximum gradient **4.984 × 10^-5** and a positive-definite
Hessian. The retrospective terminal years **2016 and 2019** exceed this
project's strict 10^-4 gradient criterion despite their recorded `OK` status.
The posterior table reports maximum R-hat **1.075**, minimum bulk ESS **36.0**,
and minimum tail ESS **21.7**; its own targets are R-hat ≤ 1.01 and ESS ≥ 400.
Resolve mixing and effective sample size before importing draws into the OM.
The published projection configuration uses F40% and F35% in a Tier 3 development
check. It explicitly retains the accepted assessment for management advice.

The newer local working exports have a different objective and diagnostic profile.
Their source fingerprints are recorded alongside the live hashes. These versions
must be reconciled to one designated run before an assessment-to-OM export.
The local working results also exceed their posterior diagnostic targets.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-model26-versions
#| tbl-cap: "Published and local working diagnostics, kept as separate evidence versions. These are imported diagnostics; no model was refit for this review."
read.csv("site/data/model26_source_comparison.csv") |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_scientific(columns = max_gradient, decimals = 3) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(max_rhat, min_bulk_ess, min_tail_ess), decimals = 3) |>
  cols_label(source = "Version", max_gradient = "Max gradient", pd_hessian = "PD Hessian",
             max_rhat = "Max R-hat", min_bulk_ess = "Min bulk ESS", min_tail_ess = "Min tail ESS",
             retros_exceeding_1e4 = "Retros over 1e-4")
```
